report.source_text: Three weeks later, the patient showed subjective and objective improvement in ocular symptoms. Visual acuity improved to 20/20 bilaterally, with normal IOP. Slit lamp examination revealed clear and unremarkable anterior segments bilaterally. Mild lower vitritis (0.5 + cells) was found in both eyes. Fundus examination revealed mild elevation and slight blurring of the nasal optic disc bilaterally. In the right eye, the macula appeared dry with two small, pinpoint, paracentral well-defined hypopigmented foci and no signs of inflammation in the peripheral retina. In the left eye, a dry macula with a small hypopigmented focus was located nasally to the fovea, and there was no inflammation on the periphery.

report.source_text: Two months after the initial presentation, the patient showed further ocular improvement. Visual acuity was stable, and fundus examination of both eyes revealed few cells in the lower vitreous cavity with unremarkable discs and dry macula (Fig. 2A). OCT of both eyes revealed prominent improvement with preserved contours and fewer retinal hyperreflective foci with preserved photoreceptor layers (Fig. 2B). He was advised to discontinue prednisone with further follow-up in our ophthalmology clinic.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 24-year-old male soldier presented with a 2-week systemic prodrome of fever (39°C), headaches, night sweats, transient rash, and 10 kg weight loss, followed by ocular manifestations: right eye paracentral scotoma (7-day history) and left eye scattered dark spots (2-day history). Fundoscopic examination on admission revealed bilateral mild optic disc elevation and blurriness nasally with yellowish foci consistent with retinitis adjacent to the fovea in both eyes, consistent with bilateral retinochoroiditis and vitritis. Laboratory investigations showed thrombocytosis without leukocytosis, elevated atypical lymphocytes, elevated liver enzymes, and elevated ESR (24 mm/hr), with positive Rickettsia typhi serology and negative toxoplasmosis and syphilis serology. The patient was treated with doxycycline 100 mg twice daily and prednisone 50 mg daily. At 3 weeks post-treatment, visual acuity improved to 20/20 bilaterally with mild residual vitritis (0.5+ cells) and fundoscopic findings showing hypopigmented foci consistent with resolving retinitis. At 2 months post-treatment, ocular improvement continued with stable visual acuity, few cells in the lower vitreous, unremarkable discs, dry macula, and OCT showing preserved photoreceptor layers with fewer hyperreflective foci.
